definitions.explanation: A simple side-blown bamboo flute used in folk music and festival music ({祭|まつ}り{囃子|ばやし}). Sweeter and lighter than the more formal {龍笛|りゅうてき} of gagaku.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りで{篠笛|しのぶえ}を{聴|き}いた。
examples.english: I heard a shinobue at the festival.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{篠笛|しのぶえ}を{習|なら}い{始|はじ}めた。
{篠笛|しのぶえ}の{澄|す}んだ{音色|ねいろ}が{境内|けいだい}に{響|ひび}いた。
examples.english: The clear tone of the shinobue echoed through the shrine grounds.

notes:
Made from {篠竹|しのだけ} (a kind of slender bamboo). Used in folk music, kabuki, festival music, and increasingly in modern compositions. Comes in a range of keys, identified by a number ({一本調子|いっぽんちょうし}, {二本調子|にほんちょうし}, etc.).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {篠笛|しのぶえ}を{吹|ふ}く: to play the shinobue
- {篠笛|しのぶえ}の{音色|ねいろ}: the tone of the shinobue
- {祭|まつ}りの{篠笛|しのぶえ}: shinobue at a festival

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {龍笛|りゅうてき}: ryuteki — transverse flute of gagaku; more formal, used in court music
- {尺八|しゃくはち}: shakuhachi — end-blown bamboo flute, used in Zen and folk music
